I also noticed that my QUOTAGUARDSTATIC_URL variable has different host and port than it's in your docs - I'm assuming that docs are a bit outdated, but wanted to confirm.

Any help would be appreciated.

subject: SOCKS logging for FTPS traffic
description:
Hello,

I'm working on implementing QuotaGuard with SOCKS for FTPS requests to a third party server.  I recently moved to Heroku, and I'm having trouble implementing this with a SOCKS proxy enabled in conjunction with the dobule-bag-ftps gem (https://github.com/bnix/double-bag-ftps), as all requests timing out.  I followed the steps for downloading the socksify wrapper and updating my Profile.  Another peculiarity with this process (though not sure if related), all of my web requests to the Heroku instance after updating my Procfile caused my instance to fail starting up unless I specifically set a `QUOTAGUARDSTATIC_MASK` value to the domain names for which I require this on outbound traffic.

My big question is: why are my FTP requests timing out despite the host ("example.c1data.com") matching the `QUOTAGUARDSTATIC_MASK` domain value (".c1data.com,.ziggidycreative.com"), and why am I not seeing anything in the QuotaGuard logs even after an hour for SOCKS request updates?

Thank you,
Matt Huggins

subject: Connection Timeout
description:
I was speaking with Tim yesterday regarding connecting to a MySQL instance through a static IP allocated to us via QuotaGuard.

I've updated my foreman file to begin the webserver as follows:
bin/qgsocksify bundle exec unicorn -p $PORT -c ./config/unicorn.rb

In my heroku config, I have the following:
QUOTAGUARDSTATIC_URL: http://quotaguard2307:554d294d6fd3@us-east-1-static-brooks.quotaguard.com:9293

However, when I start up my server, it appears to timeout. Error R10 (Boot timeout) -> Web process failed to bind to $PORT within 60 seconds of launch

I dug a bit deeper and noticed that in the setup for Rails you guys mentioned specifying the connection_timeout as nil. 
https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/quotaguardstatic#setting-up-mysql-access-from-rails

Is this something that is required?

When I run the rails console (heroku run rails console), I am able to access my database.

When I run `heroku run bin/qgsocksify curl -L http://ip.jsontest.com/` it does return the static IP address: {"ip": "54.84.188.199"}

However, it seems there is possibly an issue starting up the unicorn server with qgsocksify. Any insight?

Brian
